What is written has been fulfilled in you: ‘A city is established through the wisdom of a strong man, but it is also demolished through the foolishness of a fool.’”
When the man heard these things, he fell facedown, saying, “Forgive me, my lord, holy martyr!
I have sinned beyond the measure of all humanity.
Do not hold my foolishness against me, and I will be your faithful servant, like my father, until the day of my death.
I pledge to your holy glory that if you have mercy on me and forgive my insolence, I will give half my property and my crops to your sanctuary every year.
The other half will go toward my taxes and the livelihood of my workers. And as for the other acts of mercy that my father performs for the poor,
I will add to them.” The holy man said to him, “God has taken away your sin, and this will be a sign for you:
When you get up early tomorrow morning, open the doors of your storehouses and taste your wines.
You will find that they have been restored to their former condition, so that you may know that God has power over everything.”
And it is God's blessing that makes a person rich, but it is a person's willingness that God loves.
For he does not need your love or your offering, but he wants your goodwill toward him.
Have you not heard what is written: “Whoever is kind to the poor lends to God,” and, “Fulfill your vows to God”?
Everyone around him will bring him gifts.
Now, then, take care to carry out what has come from your mouth.
And I will plead with the Lord on your behalf, so that he may increase your wealth as he did your father's.
And when you leave the body, your soul will not be separated from his, because I received him as a gift in God's presence, and he gave him the good things of the kingdom of heaven.
Have you not heard what is written: “The prayer of a righteous person is very powerful and effective”?
Do you think the martyrs endured these sufferings for nothing?
Now, then, my son, watch yourself from this day forward, and you will be saved.
When the saint had said these things to him, he stopped seeing him.
Immediately he awoke from the vision, trembling. He told his people what he had seen, and they were amazed.
And when morning came, he opened the door of his storehouses.
He found that his wines were exceptionally fine, and he was astonished.
He proclaimed the miracles of Saint Victor throughout the whole city.
He summoned the steward of the saint's shrine.
He gave him half of his produce and his wine to distribute for the needs of the shrine, the poor, and strangers, just as he had promised the saint.
And from that day on, he became a devoted man, attending to the salvation of his soul.
You have seen, my beloved, how great are the miracles of Saint Victor, whose feast we celebrate today.
And my feeble tongue cannot recount even one ten-thousandth of his virtues, his honor, and the wonders he performed.
Let us celebrate his feast today with purity of heart and purity of body. He is able to intercede for us before the Lord, so that he may forgive us our sins.
For he is merciful, and he is close to God at all times.
Let us keep ourselves away from every evil and every wicked act.
Let us not persist in sin, so that our visitation does not come to nothing.
Remember that the world will pass away along with its desires, but whoever does God's will shall remain forever.
Therefore, do not place your confidence in an empty hope.
For the apostle said, “A hope that is seen is not hope”—namely, the wealth of this world, which will pass away like a spider’s web.
Do not be an oppressor, for no oppressor will inherit the kingdom of God.
Do not be quarrelsome, for it has been said, “There is no benefit in any quarrel.”
Do not be a lover of money, for the love of money is the root of every evil.
Do not be sexually immoral, for God will destroy anyone who defiles the temple of God.
Do not be a liar, for the Lord will destroy everyone who tells lies.
Do not be a drunkard, for no drunkard will inherit the kingdom of God.
Do not be lustful, for it has been said, “Anyone who looks at a woman and desires her has already committed adultery with her in his heart.”
Do not be an adulterer, for an adulterer will destroy his own soul.
Do not be a lover of pleasure, for it is written, “They love pleasure more than they love God.”
Do not be a slanderer, for a bridle of fire will be put in the mouth of anyone who slanders.
Do not hate your brother, for anyone who hates his brother is a murderer.
Do not be double-tongued, for double-tongued speech is a double-edged sword.
If you guard yourself against these things, you will become a servant of the Lord, and Saint Victor will rejoice over the person who celebrates his feast.
Let us stretch out our hands to the poor with mercy and compassion, for it is written, “Blessed are the merciful, for they will receive mercy.”
Let us visit the sick and those who are imprisoned, so that God may visit us in his compassion.
Let us clothe the naked, so that we may escape the terror of the gnashing of teeth.
Let us welcome into our homes the poor who have no home, during the feast of Saint Victor, so that he may remember us before the Lord and bring us into his kingdom in heaven.
Let us not keep any grudge in our hearts against anyone during the feast of Saint Victor,
so that God and his angels may be among us as we celebrate his feast, lest he put us to shame as enemies.
Instead, let us loosen every bond of injustice, and put away all hostility and all malice toward one another, so that God and his holy angels may be reconciled with us.
And now, then, let us bring the discourse to a close here, for the time has come for us to present the holy offering.
The discourse calls for much more from us, but one can never have enough of the words of God and the mighty deeds of the saints.
May Saint Victor, whose feast we celebrate today, intercede with the Lord for us, so that he may forgive us our sins.
And may he bless the God-loving king and all the orthodox people.
Through Jesus Christ our Lord, through whom glory belongs to him, together with his good Father and the holy, life-giving Spirit,
who is of the same essence, now and always, through all the unending ages of ages.
Bless us. Amen. May it be so.
Through the diligence and care of the most God-loving deacon Pourot,
he took care of this book and donated it to the church of Saint Mercurius at Tbo, Apollonia in the language of Alexandria.
Lord, preserve the life and salvation of the God-loving brother [?] Pourot, and make him worthy of the joy of the kingdom of heaven.
And may he perfect him in the angelic life that he has put on, like our fathers, the founders of the community. May his blessing come down upon us, together with that of all the saints. Amen.
May the Lord Jesus Christ, truly our true God, preserve the life and salvation of the most devout archpriest Apa Abraham,
the superior and administrator of the monastery of Saint Mercurius at Tbo. May his blessing come down upon us.
Lord, preserve the life and salvation of all the fathers and sons of the monastery. May he make us worthy of their blessings and give health to our hearts.
And may they pray for me before our King, Christ, so that he may forgive my many sins and have mercy on me on the day of my visitation.
I, Joseph, the least and most wretched, the son of the blessed Sisinnius,
the archdeacon of the catholic church of Saint John the Baptist in the city of Esna.
Lord, grant him rest.
[?], the least deacon, son of Joseph the deacon. Pray for me, the wretched [?] Barachis. 99.
